gold_patch_assessment: The gold patch correctly addresses all requirements in the issue: (1) adds deleteItems and deleteInsights to Memory interface and DefaultMemory with correct vector-then-store ordering, retriever notification, and empty-collection short-circuit; (2) refactors MemoryStore to batch-oriented operations with clearer naming (e.g., getAllItems→listItems, saveInsight→upsertInsights, addItems→insertItems, etc.); (3) removes memoryId from MemoryInsightType record, making insight types global; (4) updates MemoryAutoConfiguration to require MemoryVector; (5) updates all call sites across extraction, retrieval, store implementations, converters, and seeder.
base_vs_gold_expectation: The test patch applies cleanly to the base but references renamed methods (listInsights, getInsightsByType, upsertInsights, etc.) and updated constructor signatures (MemoryInsightType without memoryId, DefaultMemory with MemoryVector) that do not exist in the base code. Without the gold patch, compilation will fail and all 12 test classes will not run, yielding a non-zero exit code. With the gold patch, the new API surface exists and tests should compile and pass. The verifier correctly accepts the gold patch and rejects the unmodified base.
too_narrow_risks: No test for empty collection edge case on deleteItems or deleteInsights (issue explicitly requires 'Empty id collections should complete without doing work')
No test for duplicate vectorId deduplication in deleteItems (gold patch uses .distinct() on vectorIds but this is not tested)
No direct test that DefaultTaxonomySeeder uses the global upsertInsightTypes instead of per-memory saveInsightType
No test for the MybatisPlusMemoryStore.deleteInsights batch operation (only InMemoryMemoryStore.deleteInsights is tested)
too_broad_risks: Tests include 12 test classes spanning extraction, retrieval, tracing, and auto-config — some only verify method renames rather than new functionality, which makes the test suite sensitive to unrelated changes in those areas
implementation_coupling: The InOrder verification in DefaultMemoryTest.deleteItemsDeletesVectorsThenStoreRowsAndInvalidatesRetriever checks a specific call sequence (getItemsByIds → deleteBatch → deleteItems → onDataChanged) which matches the issue spec but constrains the reactive chain structure slightly — an implementation that batches differently but achieves the same observable result could fail
Tests check for exact method calls on mocks (e.g., verifyNoInteractions(vector)) which is behavior-coupling rather than implementation-coupling, but still somewhat constraining
environment_risks: Maven build requires pre-cached dependencies in the Docker image; if the image is missing any transitive dependency, network access may be needed
MybatisPlusMemoryStoreBatchOperationsTest uses @TempDir for SQLite files which depends on temp directory availability
The 3600s verifier timeout is generous but the full Maven build + 12 test classes across 4 modules could be slow on constrained environments

evidence.detail: base_commit 6f9a4c6 matches HEAD of /testbed, confirming correct repository state

Test patch adds 3 new deletion-specific tests in DefaultMemoryTest (lines 60-108), 1 new InMemoryMemoryStoreTest file (lines 706-883), 1 new InsightTypeConverterTest file (lines 1043-1131), and 2 new MemoryAutoConfigurationTest tests including MemoryVector requirement check
Base MemoryStore uses old method names (getAllItems, saveInsight, getAllInsightTypes, etc.) confirming test patch references to renamed methods will fail compilation without gold patch
Base MemoryInsightType record has memoryId field (line 25), confirming constructor calls in test patch without memoryId will fail compilation without gold patch
MemoryVector.deleteBatch already exists in base (line 63), so gold patch correctly relies on existing API for vector deletion
eval.sh runs 12 specific test classes across 4 Maven modules with -Dtest filter, appropriately scoped to affected areas

summary: This is a well-constructed benchmark instance. The gold patch comprehensively addresses the issue (deletion APIs, store refactoring, global insight types, auto-config changes). The test patch provides good coverage of the core new behavior (deleteItems ordering and vector-skip logic, deleteInsights, auto-config MemoryVector requirement) plus adapts existing tests to the renamed API surface. Tests are primarily behavior-oriented rather than implementation-coupled. Minor gaps exist: no test for empty-collection short-circuit and no test for MybatisPlusMemoryStore.deleteInsights. The verifier correctly discriminates between base and gold-patched code because the test patch references renamed methods that only exist after the gold patch.
